_comment: Attachment risk, judged from metadata only. The parser hashes attachment bytes
and discards them, so nothing here can inspect content - no archive is opened, no
macro is extracted, nothing is executed. That is a deliberate limit, not a gap:
the platform never needs to hold a malware sample to say a .exe arrived.
`executable` extensions run code on a double-click. `macro` formats carry code
that a prompt can be talked into enabling. `container` formats are the standard
way to smuggle either past a scanner, and are also how the mark-of-the-web is
stripped so Windows stops warning about the file inside.
`expected_types` maps an extension to the MIME types a legitimate sender declares
for it. A mismatch means the sender's own client disagrees with the filename,
which is either misconfiguration or disguise.
